summary: Coding and modernization conventions for migrating VB6 banking application to C# with emphasis on naming, error handling, testing, logging, auth, API, and security.

rules.rule: Use PascalCase for all class names, method names, and public properties in C# modernization.

provenance.evidence: Legacy VB6 uses PascalCase for forms and modules; C# standard is PascalCase.

rules.rule: Use structured exception handling (try-catch) in C# to replace VB6 error handling patterns.

provenance.evidence: Legacy VB6 code uses On Error statements; modern C# uses exceptions.

rules.rule: Develop comprehensive unit tests for all business logic migrated from VB6 modules to C# classes.
examples: NUnit or MSTest test classes covering deposit and withdrawal logic
counterexamples: No tests or manual testing only

provenance.evidence: Legacy code lacks automated tests; modernization requires test coverage.

rules.rule: Implement centralized logging using a framework like Serilog or NLog in the modernized C# application.

provenance.evidence: Legacy VB6 code has no structured logging; modernization should improve observability.

rules.rule: Passwords must be securely handled and stored using salted hashing algorithms; do not store plaintext passwords as in legacy forms.
examples: Use ASP.NET Identity or similar for authentication
counterexamples: Storing passwords in plain text or reversible encryption

provenance.evidence: Legacy form uses PasswordChar but no evidence of secure storage.

rules.rule: Expose business logic via RESTful APIs with JSON payloads for integration and UI decoupling.
counterexamples: Monolithic UI-bound logic with no API layer

provenance.evidence: Legacy VB6 is monolithic; modernization requires API layer.

rules.rule: Use parameterized queries or ORM frameworks to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities during database access modernization.
examples: Using Dapper or Entity Framework with parameters
counterexamples: Concatenating SQL strings with user input

provenance.evidence: Legacy uses DAO/ADO with potential concatenated SQL queries.

lint_recommendations: Enforce PascalCase naming for all identifiers
Disallow use of legacy VB6 error handling constructs
Require unit test coverage for all migrated modules
Mandate use of secure password storage and authentication frameworks
Enforce parameterized queries for all database access
scaffold_templates: C# class template with exception handling and logging
REST API controller template using ASP.NET Core
Unit test project template using MSTest or NUnit
Secure authentication service template using ASP.NET Identity
